recent_notebooks.title: AI Dependence and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes

retrieval_triggers: sign that an excerpt may hide a material distinction

review.alternative: The association could be bidirectional, with athletes prone to outsourcing seeking AI tools to justify existing tendencies.
review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal data showing that initial body signal sensitivity does not predict subsequent AI dependence.

claims.statement: AI training recommendation dependence is positively associated with body signal outsourcing.

support.explanation: This establishes the initial link in the serial association model.
support.passage: AI training recommendation dependence was significantly and positively associated with body signal outsourcing tendency

review.alternative: Training decision hesitation might arise from overtraining or physical exhaustion independent of AI reliance.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that athletes with high AI dependence maintain high self-efficacy scores.

claims.statement: Body signal outsourcing leads to reduced self-regulation, increased training decision hesitation, and reduced training self-efficacy in a serial pathway.

support.explanation: The chain of psychological consequences is empirically supported by the structural equation modeling results.
support.passage: A reduced sense of self-regulation was positively associated with training decision hesitation, which was further positively associated with reduced training self-efficacy.

actions.findings:
AI training recommendation dependence is positively associated with body signal outsourcing. [source-43e60aa546c849b2]

Body signal outsourcing leads to reduced self-regulation, increased training decision hesitation, and reduced training self-efficacy in a serial pathway. [source-43e60aa546c849b2]
actions.limitations: Current findings are based on cross-sectional data; the proposed serial association requires longitudinal validation to confirm causal directionality.
actions.next_questions: To what extent do these autonomy-reducing effects vary between novice and elite athletes, and can intervention strategies mitigate the outsourcing tendency while maintaining the benefits of AI-driven rigor?
actions.reason: Revision incorporates new structural equation modeling results validating the serial association between AI dependence and reduced training self-efficacy.
actions.summary: Evidence indicates that AI training recommendation dependence functions as a serial mediator in reducing athlete training self-efficacy. This occurs through a pathway: dependence on AI recommendations increases body signal outsourcing, which lowers self-regulation, leading to increased decision hesitation and ultimately lower self-efficacy.
actions.title: AI Dependency and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes

proposal.summary: Updated findings regarding the serial association between AI training recommendation dependence, body signal outsourcing, self-regulation, and training self-efficacy in athletes.
proposal.title: Synthesis of AI-Dependency in Athletic Training
